Pool scamster JP Mostert

By: Este de Klerk | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Maybe swimming in ground is a new sport we just haven't heard of? One that goes with paying a guy to build you a very expensive hole in the ground? He's back: JP Mostert, or maybe just never left.

Summary:
Maybe swimming in ground is a new sport we just haven't heard of? One that goes with paying a guy to build you a very expensive hole in the ground? He's back: JP Mostert of Rock & Pools Creations, Tropikana, Decro Construction, Decro Water Proofing & Constructions, Decro Thatch and Pools... or maybe he just never left.



Further information:
In 2010 we asked: "Want a new pool, koi dam or lapa? Water features and a beautiful garden? Look no further. To avoid a tedious search and several contractors at your house at the same time, just call the number of this one-stop shop on the East Rand in Gauteng. They promise to deliver professional service."

At the time JP Mostert was operating under a company with the name of Rock and Pools Creations.
He promises the world and that your dream pool and garden will be created without a fuss and in a tiffy.
Contract, no contract, you can trust him, and people do...

He quotes and asks for a 60 - 80 percent deposit upfront. Once the deposit is paid, he and his workers arrives immediately and starts to works at a massive tempo. They do this for a day or two.
Then he asks for more money, often in cash, to buy additional material needed.
Once he has this money in his pocket, he stays away. Maybe comes back for an extra day or so. Then he disappears.
The client calls him excessively to ask when he will be finishing the job. He doesn't answer.
He only responds to whatsapp messages, with excuses of why he cannot complete the job now.
Excuses range from: he is busy with another job and will come once the job is finished, his workers didn't pitch because it was raining; it is raining and he can't work in the rain; it was raining and the pool needs time to dry; he is in hospital...
He used the same excuses four years ago when we did the story about him.

Then he makes promises: he will deliver the material the next day.
That doesn't happen. Next message: he will deliver it in a week.
Next promise: He could not deliver, but client must give him a few more days to sort out his things and he will deliver it the next week.

Once the clients is fed-up with his promises and non-delivery and tells him that he will go to the police and write reports on all social media, JP starts to threaten the clients.
Threats range from: I hope you and you family have a nice week (with a picture of a skeleton face); I hope you sleep well; I will break all the fucking bones in your body; you won't get away with this; I give you one day to take it off (social media) or... lol; you've investigated me, so I won't finish the job and you will never see your money again.

After we did the story in 2010 when he operated on the East Rand, he moved to Cape Town, Durban and Thabazimbi and then zoomed in on Gautang again, now tackling the Vaal triangle.

Currently there is about 20 criminal charges laid against him at the police and the Director of Public Prosecutions in the Free State is considering a decision to prosecute or not.

Press Release:


Pool Con
With summer holidays around the corner, dreams of new swimming pools, lapas and beautiful water features abound. But how do you know that the contractor who takes your deposit and promises to turn your dreams into reality won’t disappear, leaving a very expensive hole in the ground? Carte Blanche hears from consumers left between a rock and a hard place.


Script:


POOL CON/JP MOSTERT

PRODUCER: ESTé DE KLERK

DEREK LINK: Andre Bezuidenhout paid nearly R190 000 to refurbish his pool and pave the surroundings. He had to get another company in to finish the pool and there is no paving.

DEREK LINK: David Meyers handed over cheques for more than a R150 000 in one week. He was left with a concrete shell crumbling and cracked and another company has to sort it out.

The contractor responsible for the unfinished projects: JP Mostirt… or Jean-Pierre Mostert as per his ID book… or Juan - a name he recently used when intruding himself to clients.

In 2010, he worked under the company name Rock & Pools Creations, then later under Tropicana Decks and Pools and in the past few months he’s done business, mainly in the Vaal Triangle area, as Decro Construction and Decro Water Proofing and Construction.

DEREK LINK: There we go: pools and ponds, ….but it seems that not everything is going so swimmingly well in the pools that they promise to build.

LOUIS STRAPP/FORMER CLIENT: 10:40 He arrived here in a fairly new Ford Everest car, he has a thing on his phone that does all the measurements, good advice, he rather build pools, very trustworthy kind of guy

ANDRE BEZUIDENHOUT: The talk sounded good. He sounded like he technically knew what he was talking about when it comes to pools.

IAN VAN DER WATT: He came with a soothing attitude, you know, he put you at ease when talking to you. So, we didn’t have anything to worry about.

It sounds like good business practice – being prompt and having your clients’ best interests at heart.
But does some of it sound too good to be true?

LOUIS STRAPP: He mentioned to me that he’s got a friend that is either moving or immigrating and he wanted to sell off his heater pump before he moved and he said that this heater pump cost around R20 000 new and he could organise it for me for about R6500, but on one condition: that he had the money for the heater pump upfront.

So impressed with JP’s good advice, Louis from Vanderbijlpark, paid over R55 000 upfront.
This payment went towards the heater pump, a new pool, wooden decking and a wall.
Louis was particularly taken with JP’s special offers, which even included plants from a nursery in Pretoria that JP said belonged to his uncle.

LOUIS STRAPP: He says: “ Let’s use the remaining amount and do something special. He would like to use this house as an advertisement.” Then he came up with a couple of suggestions saying that he would build an extra wall for me, he would include a whole lot of sandstone-cladding, put in two nice Cycads for me.

Andre was also taken in by the charming JP – he wanted to install a new pool pump.

ANDRE BEZUIDENHOUT: I felt I was getting good, prompt service. Once the pump was delivered, I asked him to just have a look at the pool, because it was in need of a bit of maintenance.

DEREK: How much have you paid him?

ANDRE BEZUIDENHOUT: In total, I have paid him R190 000.

DEREK: But why have you paid him so much in advance?

ANDRE BEZUIDENHOUT: He convinced me he could get the materials at a certain good price but I had to move now.

At Dave and Trudie Meyers’ house in Sasolburg, another pool-make-over was in progress. With Dave in Saudi Arabia, Trudie and future son-in-law, Ian van der Watt met JP. They had big plans for their entertainment area.

DEREK: Now, you ended up paying more than a R150 000. What did you get for that?

IAN VAN DER WATT: A great big hole in our yard. A big mess left afterwards.

DEREK: Why did you terminate his services?

IAN VAN DER WATT: We did not terminate his services: he just never pitched up again.

JP MOSTERT: Juan, hallo?

DEREK: Hi, is that JP?

JP MOSTERT: Speaking, how can I help you?

DEREK: Hi, this is Derek Watts from Carte Blanche.

JP MOSTERT: Yes Derek.

DEREK: JP, we’ve received some complaints from pool customers and we’d like to speak to you on camera.

JP MOSTERT: I am only going to be back that side, Johannesburg-side, it’s about about only in two-week’s time though.

DEREK: Where are you at the moment?

JP: In Paternoster.

DEREK: JP, if we come down to Cape Town, can we see you in Paternoster.

JP: No problem, that is fine as well.

But a few minutes later he called back to decline an on-camera interview. Within hours, we established that he was not in Paternoster, but in Durban. His foreman, Carlos, also confirmed this.

VOICE: Where is JP?

CARLOS: He’s there by Durban.

VOICE: Is JP in Durban?

CARLOS: Yes.

DEREK LINK: If this all sounds familiar, then maybe you are not imagining things. We did a story on JP Mostert in 2010 and it seems that history is repeating itself.

[CARTE BLANCHE FEBRUARY 2010]
APRIL WOODS-CLEGG: He would not take the call, or he would argue his case about the jackhammers being stolen.

ROBBYN BURGER: A hundred and one excuses – his house was robbed, his sister was in hospital.

When Andre told JP that he’d discovered he’d been exposed on Carte Blanche in the past, JP said that was his cousin, and definitely not him.
But by then, Andre had seen right through him.

ANDRE: He would always have a story. Once he was in hospital for a day…

LOUIS: His bakkies are in for service, he got stuck in the traffic…

IAN: The trailor would break, or the prop shafts of the vehicle would break.

ANDRE: He’s just picking up his tools at another property…

LOUIS: And I think he just couldn’t remember who he had told what.

DEREK: We’ve spoken to nine people who say that they’ve paid upfront and you haven’t delivered?

JP: Ja no, I was busy working there when they cancelled the work. So, you can just get response from them as well. I was busy working there when Dave Meyers went to them and he told them about my story on the previous Carte Blanche and they cancelled the work, yes.

JP claims Dave Meyers did this because JP had broken up with his daughter, Mandy.

JP: Dave Meyers, like I told, he went to the police. I was with his daughter, Mandy. When I left her, he started making problems and cancelled the work.

Dave, who works in Saudi Arabia, denies all these claims. “I did not end JP Mostert’s services. He ended it with me.”

Dave also said: “Mandy ended the relationship, not Mostert.

DEREK: But JP, the people that we have spoken to say that David never approached them.

JP: No, they did. They did. And I got proof of it as well.

DEREK: Can you send us that proof.

JP: He definitely did approach them, there’s no way he didn’t approach them.

JP never sent us the proof.
Dave denies ever approaching JP’s clients and Andre and Louis say they’ve never had any contact with Dave.

Louis, in fact, heard about JP’s shenanigans from his local pool shop.

LOUIS: I just enquired from one of the workers if they knew this JP Mostert that was doing pools and this guy had a surprised look on his face and he says: “Why, are you dealing with JP Mostert?” And they say I hope you haven’t been caught by him as well.

ANDRE: The modus operandi, it appears, is that he move from area to area. He would feel the heat at a point in time and then he move one. You would find that he defrauded people in the Western Cape, in fact, there is a judgment against him for R72 000 in the Strand Magistrates Court.

When JP’s clients started to challenge and expose him, the threats started to fly.

DEREK: Some of your clients say that you’ve threatened them.

JP: That is a bull*** story as well. If you can proof it to you, that is fine.

DEREK: Well, we’ve got some of the threats on Whatsapp, been printed out.

JP: Ok cool that is fine, I didn’t threaten in any way.

ANDRE: When I said to him I am going to the media with this, that got him very, very upset. He then, via Whatsapp said to me that if I do that, I would lose everything.

IAN: My mother-in-law speaking on the phone with him, I in the background shouted: “You don’t know what you are doing, you don’t know what you are talking about.” And he immediately just lost it and started threatening me and told me, or in an sms told me that if I want to have a long healthy life, I should just keep my mouth off of him.

ANDRE: He had an undercover threat made on Whatsapp as well, where he says: “I believe you love your family very much, have an awesome week.” And then a follow-up sms where he is basically saying I need to remove whatever I’ve said and done, undo that within ten minutes or it will be game on.

DEREK: Are you nervous about this?

ANDRE: Yes, I am. We went as far as arranging extra security for the day.

When Louis demanded to see JP, he threatened Louis over the phone.

LOUIS: He says: “Well, if I come over there, I will break every bloody bone in your body.” And I said: “Why would you do that? You got almost R60 000 of my money!”

Last Sunday, JP contacted some of his clients to say that he would start to pay them back in instalments from Wednesday.

DEREK: Why are you offering to pay back some clients?

JP: I said I would pay their money, because I stopped working there, because they cancelled and I don’t want their phone calls all the time.

None of JP’s clients we were in touch with, received these promised re-payments.

DEREK LINK: In the last programme, JP promised to pay back Robbyn Burger the R35 000 he owed her. We called Robbyn to find out what had transpired since then.

VOICE OF ROBBYN BURGER: He’s never paid us back a single cent in the past five years.

DEREK: JP, back in 2010, you promised to pay back Robbyn Burger, five years later she still hasn’t got that 35K?

JP: Yes, not. Because you put me on Carte Blanche and everything. And I’ve lost track of her long time ago.

Andre, Louis and Dave have opened criminal cases against JP.

DEREK LINK: The police have confirmed that a total of fifteen criminal charges have been laid against JP at stations from Thabazimbi to Sasolburg.

LT HANI: Six of those are opened here with us, Sasolburg SAPS, and at the moment it has been sent to Bloemfontein to the Director of Public Prosecution who will decide to prosecute or not.

DEREK: What are the charges?

LT HANI: Theft under false pretences.

JP maintains his innocence.

JP: I don’t care, I know in anywat that I am going to be the wrong one again, so I don’t care. So, put it on, it is fine. I know I am not wrong in most of the ways.

Louis was particularly taken with JP’s special offers, which even included plants from a nursery in Pretoria that JP said belonged to his uncle. LOUIS STRAPP: He says: “ Let’s use the remaining amount and do something special. He would like to use this house as an advertisement.” Then he came up with a couple of suggestions saying that he would build an extra wall for me, he would include a whole lot of sandstone-cladding, put in two nice Cycads for me. Andre was also taken in by the charming JP – he wanted to install a new pool pump. ANDRE BEZUIDENHOUT: I felt I was getting good, prompt service. Once the pump was delivered, I asked him to just have a look at the pool, because it was in need of a bit of maintenance. DEREK: How much have you paid him? ANDRE BEZUIDENHOUT: In total, I have paid him R190 000. DEREK: But why have you paid him so much in advance? ANDRE BEZUIDENHOUT: He convinced me he could get the materials at a certain good price but I had to move now. At Dave and Trudie Meyers’ house in Sasolburg, another pool-make-over was in progress. With Dave in Saudi Arabia, Trudie and future son-in-law, Ian van der Watt met JP. They had big plans for their entertainment area. DEREK: Now, you ended up paying more than a R150 000. What did you get for that? IAN VAN DER WATT: A great big hole in our yard. A big mess left afterwards. DEREK: Why did you terminate his services? IAN VAN DER WATT: We did not terminate his services: he just never pitched up again. JP MOSTERT: Juan, hallo? DEREK: Hi, is that JP? JP MOSTERT: Speaking, how can I help you? DEREK: Hi, this is Derek Watts from Carte Blanche. JP MOSTERT: Yes Derek. DEREK: JP, we’ve received some complaints from pool customers and we’d like to speak to you on camera. JP MOSTERT: I am only going to be back that side, Johannesburg-side, it’s about about only in two-week’s time though. DEREK: Where are you at the moment? JP: In Paternoster. DEREK: JP, if we come down to Cape Town, can we see you in Paternoster. JP: No problem, that is fine as well. But a few minutes later he called back to decline an on-camera interview. Within hours, we established that he was not in Paternoster, but in Durban. His foreman, Carlos, also confirmed this. VOICE: Where is JP? CARLOS: He’s there by Durban. VOICE: Is JP in Durban? CARLOS: Yes. DEREK LINK: If this all sounds familiar, then maybe you are not imagining things. We did a story on JP Mostert in 2010 and it seems that history is repeating itself. [CARTE BLANCHE FEBRUARY 2010] APRIL WOODS-CLEGG: He would not take the call, or he would argue his case about the jackhammers being stolen. ROBBYN BURGER: A hundred and one excuses – his house was robbed, his sister was in hospital. When Andre told JP that he’d discovered he’d been exposed on Carte Blanche in the past, JP said that was his cousin, and definitely not him. But by then, Andre had seen right through him. ANDRE: He would always have a story. Once he was in hospital for a day… LOUIS: His bakkies are in for service, he got stuck in the traffic… IAN: The trailor would break, or the prop shafts of the vehicle would break. ANDRE: He’s just picking up his tools at another property… LOUIS: And I think he just couldn’t remember who he had told what. DEREK: We’ve spoken to nine people who say that they’ve paid upfront and you haven’t delivered? JP: Ja no, I was busy working there when they cancelled the work. So, you can just get response from them as well. I was busy working there when Dave Meyers went to them and he told them about my story on the previous Carte Blanche and they cancelled the work, yes. JP claims Dave Meyers did this because JP had broken up with his daughter, Mandy. JP: Dave Meyers, like I told, he went to the police. I was with his daughter, Mandy. When I left her, he started making problems and cancelled the work. Dave, who works in Saudi Arabia, denies all these claims. “I did not end JP Mostert’s services. He ended it with me.” Dave also said: “Mandy ended the relationship, not Mostert. DEREK: But JP, the people that we have spoken to say that David never approached them. JP: No, they did. They did. And I got proof of it as well. DEREK: Can you send us that proof. JP: He definitely did approach them, there’s no way he didn’t approach them. JP never sent us the proof. Dave denies ever approaching JP’s clients and Andre and Louis say they’ve never had any contact with Dave. Louis, in fact, heard about JP’s shenanigans from his local pool shop. LOUIS: I just enquired from one of the workers if they knew this JP Mostert that was doing pools and this guy had a surprised look on his face and he says: “Why, are you dealing with JP Mostert?” And they say I hope you haven’t been caught by him as well. ANDRE: The modus operandi, it appears, is that he move from area to area. He would feel the heat at a point in time and then he move one. You would find that he defrauded people in the Western Cape, in fact, there is a judgment against him for R72 000 in the Strand Magistrates Court. When JP’s clients started to challenge and expose him, the threats started to fly. DEREK: Some of your clients say that you’ve threatened them. JP: That is a bull*** story as well. If you can proof it to you, that is fine. DEREK: Well, we’ve got some of the threats on Whatsapp, been printed out. JP: Ok cool that is fine, I didn’t threaten in any way. ANDRE: When I said to him I am going to the media with this, that got him very, very upset. He then, via Whatsapp said to me that if I do that, I would lose everything. IAN: My mother-in-law speaking on the phone with him, I in the background shouted: “You don’t know what you are doing, you don’t know what you are talking about.” And he immediately just lost it and started threatening me and told me, or in an sms told me that if I want to have a long healthy life, I should just keep my mouth off of him. ANDRE: He had an undercover threat made on Whatsapp as well, where he says: “I believe you love your family very much, have an awesome week.” And then a follow-up sms where he is basically saying I need to remove whatever I’ve said and done, undo that within ten minutes or it will be game on. DEREK: Are you nervous about this? ANDRE: Yes, I am. We went as far as arranging extra security for the day. When Louis demanded to see JP, he threatened Louis over the phone. LOUIS: He says: “Well, if I come over there, I will break every bloody bone in your body.” And I said: “Why would you do that? You got almost R60 000 of my money!” Last Sunday, JP contacted some of his clients to say that he would start to pay them back in instalments from Wednesday. DEREK: Why are you offering to pay back some clients? JP: I said I would pay their money, because I stopped working there, because they cancelled and I don’t want their phone calls all the time. None of JP’s clients we were in touch with, received these promised re-payments. DEREK LINK: In the last programme, JP promised to pay back Robbyn Burger the R35 000 he owed her. We called Robbyn to find out what had transpired since then. VOICE OF ROBBYN BURGER: He’s never paid us back a single cent in the past five years. DEREK: JP, back in 2010, you promised to pay back Robbyn Burger, five years later she still hasn’t got that 35K? JP: Yes, not. Because you put me on Carte Blanche and everything. And I’ve lost track of her long time ago. Andre, Louis and Dave have opened criminal cases against JP. DEREK LINK: The police have confirmed that a total of fifteen criminal charges have been laid against JP at stations from Thabazimbi to Sasolburg. LT HANI: Six of those are opened here with us, Sasolburg SAPS, and at the moment it has been sent to Bloemfontein to the Director of Public Prosecution who will decide to prosecute or not. DEREK: What are the charges? LT HANI: Theft under false pretences. JP maintains his innocence. JP: I don’t care, I know in anywat that I am going to be the wrong one again, so I don’t care. So, put it on, it is fine. I know I am not wrong in most of the ways. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Maybe swimming in ground is a new sport we just haven't heard of? One that goes with paying a guy to build you a very expensive hole in the ground? He's back: JP Mostert, or maybe just never left.
metadata.Summary: Maybe swimming in ground is a new sport we just haven't heard of? One that goes with paying a guy to build you a very expensive hole in the ground? He's back: JP Mostert of Rock & Pools Creations, Tropikana, Decro Construction, Decro Water Proofing & Constructions, Decro Thatch and Pools... or maybe he just never left.
metadata.Further information: In 2010 we asked: "Want a new pool, koi dam or lapa? Water features and a beautiful garden? Look no further. To avoid a tedious search and several contractors at your house at the same time, just call the number of this one-stop shop on the East Rand in Gauteng. They promise to deliver professional service." At the time JP Mostert was operating under a company with the name of Rock and Pools Creations. He promises the world and that your dream pool and garden will be created without a fuss and in a tiffy. Contract, no contract, you can trust him, and people do... He quotes and asks for a 60 - 80 percent deposit upfront. Once the deposit is paid, he and his workers arrives immediately and starts to works at a massive tempo. They do this for a day or two. Then he asks for more money, often in cash, to buy additional material needed. Once he has this money in his pocket, he stays away. Maybe comes back for an extra day or so. Then he disappears. The client calls him excessively to ask when he will be finishing the job. He doesn't answer. He only responds to whatsapp messages, with excuses of why he cannot complete the job now. Excuses range from: he is busy with another job and will come once the job is finished, his workers didn't pitch because it was raining; it is raining and he can't work in the rain; it was raining and the pool needs time to dry; he is in hospital... He used the same excuses four years ago when we did the story about him. Then he makes promises: he will deliver the material the next day. That doesn't happen. Next message: he will deliver it in a week. Next promise: He could not deliver, but client must give him a few more days to sort out his things and he will deliver it the next week. Once the clients is fed-up with his promises and non-delivery and tells him that he will go to the police and write reports on all social media, JP starts to threaten the clients. Threats range from: I hope you and you family have a nice week (with a picture of a skeleton face); I hope you sleep well; I will break all the fucking bones in your body; you won't get away with this; I give you one day to take it off (social media) or... lol; you've investigated me, so I won't finish the job and you will never see your money again. After we did the story in 2010 when he operated on the East Rand, he moved to Cape Town, Durban and Thabazimbi and then zoomed in on Gautang again, now tackling the Vaal triangle. Currently there is about 20 criminal charges laid against him at the police and the Director of Public Prosecutions in the Free State is considering a decision to prosecute or not.
